clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: 2-proportions z-test for group differences in proportions of extreme deviations. Linear support vector classification to estimate diagnostic status. Linear regression models to associate z-scores/ADS with positive symptoms and IQ (covariate: age; with/without site as random effect). Brain Basis Set (BBS) multivariate modeling.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Macroscale neuromorphometric measures have limited utility as diagnostic biomarkers of psychosis risk, as individual-level variation in the clinical high-risk group was largely nested within healthy variation.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Variation in regional neuromorphometric measures in individuals with CHR-P was largely nested within the healthy distribution, and extreme deviations were present in similar proportions to healthy individuals. A greater proportion of CHR-P individuals had infranormal global, SV, and SA Average Deviation Scores (ADS). A higher percentage of individuals who converted to psychosis (CHR-PC) had infranormal values in temporal regions (e.g., 7.01% vs 1.38% in non-converters for right superior temporal sulcus SA). In the CHR-P group, SA ADS was weakly associated with positive symptoms (β = -0.08) and IQ (β = 0.09).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study used data from multiple sites, so residual site effects could remain despite harmonization. The data was cross-sectional and does not capture longitudinal changes which may be more informative.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Although we accounted for site effects using MRI data harmonization and tested the robustness of the results using leave-one-site-out analyses, residual effects cannot be fully excluded but are unlikely to have influenced the overall pattern of the results. The neuroimaging data of the individuals with CHR are cross-sectional and donotcapturepotentiallongitudinalchangesthatmaybemore informative. 32

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study performed extensive sensitivity analyses, including using alternate parcellation schemes (Schaefer-400), alternate modeling algorithms (Gaussian Process Regression, GAMLSS), analysis of specific CHR-P subsyndromes, alternate definitions of Average Deviation Scores, and a leave-one-site-out validation approach.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study is notable for being the largest CHR-P neuroimaging dataset to date, leveraging the ENIGMA CHR-P Working Group. It uniquely applies robust, pre-trained normative models from the very large ENIGMA Lifespan group (CentileBrain framework) to this specific clinical cohort, providing a powerful test of the normative modeling hypothesis in psychosis risk.
